news_headline: Hugging Face approached Nvidia's Huang weeks ahead of $12.9B acquisition, CEO tells CNBC
post_text:
Nvidia just paid $12.93 billion for Hugging Face, the platform where 18 million developers collaborate, share, and deploy open-source AI models. It's the chipmaker's second-largest acquisition on record, following last December's $20 billion Groq deal, and it pushes Nvidia's reach well past semiconductors into model distribution and the developer ecosystem itself.

Jensen Huang insists Hugging Face will remain an open platform and that Nvidia hardware won't be required to build on it. But owning the hub where the AI developer community lives is a different kind of leverage than selling GPUs. One company now sits at the foundation of AI compute and at the gateway to AI model access simultaneously.

WBR's piece on the antitrust offensive against Big Tech traced exactly this dynamic: how dominant firms accumulate chokepoints across the stack until the competitive question stops being market share and becomes structural control. The Nvidia-Hugging Face deal reads differently once you have that framework in mind. Full piece linked on our profile.

#AI #TechStrategy
